clue.text: Appeal for help succeeded heavy fall

parts.note: the Morse distress signal
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone calls for help after a heavy fall and gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: SOSS is a rare Chambers word for a heavy, clumsy fall or the noise of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives soss as a noun meaning a heavy, thudding tumble, a dialect word.

clue.text: Beating of drums at poser being top of the bill?

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drum roll greets a showy performer who heads the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Superstardom is the status of a celebrity whose name is headlined first on a show's poster.

clue.text: Flickering light, what inspires Prosper Mérimée?

indicators.note: to inspire literally means to breathe in or take in, so the word holds the answer inside

parts.note: spanning the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A candle's flicker gave the French author Prosper Mérimée his inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: SPERM is short for a spermaceti candle, made from whale oil. Prosper Mérimée was the French writer of Carmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm candle is one made from spermaceti, so a flickering light can be called a sperm in Chambers.

clue.text: Sailor's chart, one kept on board, sacred in a way (7, two words)

indicators.note: something kept on board is held within, so the letter goes inside the jumble
done in a way means done in some other manner, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a means one

explanation.surface: A sailor treasures one navigational chart kept aboard ship as something sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea card is the card of a mariner's compass, or a sea chart used for navigation.

clue.text: Give out helping but not on those cut?

indicators.note: 'but not' tells us to strip away the small word that follows it from the helping

explanation.surface: Someone handing out food portions, but not to those who have been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTRATI were male singers castrated before puberty to keep a high voice, hence the question mark on 'those cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were boy singers surgically castrated, so a playful description of them is people who were cut.

clue.text: Inveterate flirt embracing e.g. Italian sculptor

e.g. means for example, as in 'such as'

explanation.surface: A habitual womaniser hugs an Italian sculptor, say.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova's memoirs made his name a byword for a serial seducer and philanderer.

clue.text: Sailor plumbing spawn in Davy Jones's locker?

explanation.walkthrough: Davy Jones's locker is sailors' slang for the bottom of the sea, the grave of the drowned.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Jones's locker is the floor of the ocean, so the question mark marks a fanciful name for it.

clue.text: Flower carrier right in tow

explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow oblong garden basket, used to carry cut flowers or vegetables.

clue.text: Set of nets without opening split

clue.text: 'Ow 'Arry might refer to a cavity for lizard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ow 'Arry is How Harry in Cockney, the London accent that drops H, and it shows how to read the cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoles are small American lizards, related to iguanas, able to change their colour.

clue.text: Untidy nest I discern in hedging

clue.text: Keen praise distributed for old-style radio hostess

clue.text: The old insist on rule being kept in balance as before

indicators.note: something kept in another item is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

explanation.definitionFit: To press is to urge or insist, and Spenserian English wrote that verb as prease.

clue.text: Artist's instrument (not cherished) — one may draw staves

explanation.definitionFit: A rastrum is a five-nibbed pen for ruling the lines of a musical stave on manuscript paper.

clue.text: Basically gold-loving (6, two words)

fond means affectionate or loving

explanation.surface: A greedy person is, at heart, a lover of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Au fond is a French phrase used in English meaning at bottom, fundamentally or essentially.

clue.text: Sort of muffler Western lawman used to wrap colt, active?

clue.text: Typical of Byron, misused date introducing insolence

explanation.definitionFit: Taliped means club-footed, a deformity Byron famously had from birth.

clue.text: Daub showing girl in pub

a girl's name

clue.text: Chemical compound Tories restyled and had shortened

clue.text: Plasma substitute, and extraneous if without fringe elements

clue.text: Dreamy son absorbed in adult trend

taken as written
